metadata.scenario_context: Emily has finally been accepted into college, and her family is planning a celebration for her academic achievement.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Ukraine strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying lilies as a gift for Emily.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Emily's academic achievement party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have you thought about what we should get Emily for her celebration? I was thinking maybe some lilies... they’re really nice. 

What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Hmm... lilies are nice, but I think we should think about something more personal. Maybe a book or something that relates to her interests. It's important to show we care about her achievements, you know? What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, I get that... but lilies are still a classic choice. They symbolize purity and success. Just feels right for this occasion. 

But... I wonder if making our parents proud is really the main purpose of these celebrations. Isn’t it more about Emily?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Sure, it's about Emily, but... making our parents proud is also important. Celebrations like this show them the fruits of our hard work. I think they want to see us succeed, too. It’s like... a shared achievement. Makes everyone happy, right? But about the gift, maybe we could combine both ideas—lilies and something personal for her?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I mean, I guess that's one way to look at it... but I still feel it's not all about making our parents proud. 

Emily deserves to be celebrated for her own achievements, not just as a reflection of us. I think we should stick to the lilies. They’re beautiful. 

What do you really think about that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I get that... Emily deserves her moment. But I still believe that part of celebrating is about showing our parents that we value education and hard work. It’s *important* to honor that connection. The lilies could be nice, but I still think we should add something that reflects her personally. It’s not just about the flowers, right?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I understand what you're saying... but I still think the lilies can stand alone as a meaningful gift. 

This celebration is about Emily’s journey, not just proving anything to our parents. I mean, don’t you feel like we should focus on what Emily wants, rather than what everyone else expects?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I understand your point about Emily and her journey. But I really think that, deep down, we are all the same. We all want to celebrate success and show appreciation. It’s just part of human nature to want to make our parents proud, too. It’s not about proving anything; it’s about recognizing hard work. When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us, wanting to support and uplift each other. So maybe we can find a way to honor both Emily and that shared value?
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
I see what you're saying, but I still believe that focusing on Emily's individuality should come first. 

It's not that I don't appreciate our parents or what they want, but I just think there’s more to this. Celebrating Emily is about her, not a shared value. I’d still like to go with the lilies. They represent her success in a beautiful way.
turns.label: Acceptance

It’s not about dismissing Emily’s individuality; it’s about enhancing it with our support.
